name: Albania
tagline: Closed to the world until 1991, and now the least developed and least expensive coast on the Mediterranean.
summary: Albania spent forty years as the most isolated country in Europe, and the 173,000 concrete bunkers built during it are still in the fields. Since opening it has become the Balkans' fastest-changing destination: an Ionian coast with genuinely empty beaches, an alpine north with a working blood-feud memory and hospitality codes older than the state, and a capital painted in primary colours.

season.note: The Ionian coast works from May to October and is busy with Albanians and Kosovars in August. The northern Alps are walkable from mid-June to early October; the Valbona-Theth pass is snowbound outside that.

getting_around: Furgon minibuses run without fixed timetables and leave when full. There is almost no functioning railway. The Koman Lake ferry is the way north and is spectacular. Roads have improved enormously and are still not fast.
food: Byrek, and the argument about whose grandmother's is best
Tavë kosi: lamb baked in yoghurt, the national dish
Fresh fish on the coast at prices that will surprise you
know: Cash is still king outside Tirana; the lek is not widely obtainable abroad.
Hospitality (besa) is a genuine cultural obligation and refusing food can offend.
Mountain paths in the north are marked but rescue is limited — go with a guide or a good map.

regions.name: Tirana, the Riviera & the South
regions.summary: The painted capital, two Ottoman museum-towns, and the Ionian coast.

cities.name: Tirana
cities.summary: A capital whose mayor painted the grey communist blocks in primary colours, and where a nuclear bunker is now a museum.
highlights: Bunk'Art: Hoxha's nuclear bunker, 106 rooms, as a museum
The Pyramid, a dictator's mausoleum turned tech centre
Blloku, once closed to all but the party elite, now the bar district

experiences.name: Bunk'Art, underground
experiences.summary: A five-storey bunker built for a leadership expecting invasion that never came; the exhibition does not soften the regime.

cities.name: Gjirokastër
cities.summary: A UNESCO-listed Ottoman town of stone-roofed tower houses on a steep hillside under a castle.
highlights: Slate-roofed houses built as fortified homes
The castle, and the American spy plane parked in it
Skënduli House, still owned and shown by the family

cities.name: Himarë & the Riviera
cities.summary: Ionian villages between mountain and sea, with beaches that were empty ten years ago and are filling fast.
highlights: Gjipe beach, at the mouth of a canyon, reached on foot
The Llogara pass, dropping 1,000 metres to the sea
Fish, olive oil and citrus from the villages behind

regions.name: The Albanian Alps
regions.summary: The 'Accursed Mountains': stone villages, a ferry through a gorge, and a pass between two valleys.

cities.name: Theth
cities.summary: A valley village of stone houses with no road in until recently, a lock-in tower, and a waterfall above it.
highlights: The Valbona-Theth pass, a six-hour crossing on foot
The kulla, a tower where men under blood feud could shelter
The Blue Eye of Theth, up the river

experiences.name: The Valbona to Theth pass
experiences.summary: Six to eight hours over 1,800 metres between two valleys, with guesthouses at both ends and mules for bags.

experiences.name: The Koman Lake ferry
experiences.summary: Three hours through a flooded gorge on a working passenger boat that carries villagers, goats and the occasional car.
